newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kampo says wary of buying JGBs after yield falls.
newsitem.headline: Kampo says wary of buying JGBs after yield falls.

text.p: Falls in yen interest rates to record low levels have made Japan's Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo) more cautious about buying Japanese government bonds (JGBs), a Kampo official said on Thursday.

He told Reuters that Kampo was interested in boosting its foreign bond purchases due to the wide yield differentials between Japan and such countries as the United States and due to expectations that the dollar is unlikely to fall below 120 yen in the near term.
"We cannot be too comfortable about parking funds in yen bonds with the yield repeatedly setting record lows," the official said.
Kampo is the largest institutional investor in Japan with total assets of 97.22 trillion yen as of the end of February.
The yield on the key 182nd 10-year bond ended Tokyo's Thursday session at 2.175 percent, after falling to a record low of 2.140 percent on Wednesday.
The official said that Kampo has been trimming the weighting of JGBs in its portfolio since late last year.
"Looking at the situation for domestic interest rates, foreign bonds are more attractive," the official said.
He said that Kampo was not expecting to see the dollar weaken below 120 yen.
The latest survey of Kampo's assets showed that foreign bond holdings totalled 4.27 trillion yen, or 4.4 percent of the total.
Kampo's portfolio in JGBs and bonds from other Japanese government-related institutions stood at 35.04 trillion yen, or 36 percent of the total.
